deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE waves and optics: wave motion, sound, stationary waves, Doppler effect, mirrors, lenses, interference, diffraction, and polarization.
front: What is special about central maximum in single-slit diffraction?
back: The central maximum is brightest and widest compared with secondary maxima.
explanation: Intensity of secondary maxima decreases on both sides.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE waves and optics: wave motion, sound, stationary waves, Doppler effect, mirrors, lenses, interference, diffraction, and polarization.
front: What is a diffraction grating?
back: A diffraction grating is an optical element with many equally spaced parallel slits used to disperse light.
explanation: It produces sharp spectral lines.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE waves and optics: wave motion, sound, stationary waves, Doppler effect, mirrors, lenses, interference, diffraction, and polarization.
front: What is resolving power?
back: Resolving power is the ability of an optical instrument to distinguish two close objects or spectral lines as separate.
explanation: Higher resolving power gives clearer distinction.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE waves and optics: wave motion, sound, stationary waves, Doppler effect, mirrors, lenses, interference, diffraction, and polarization.
front: What is polarization?
back: Polarization is restriction of vibrations of a transverse wave to one plane.
explanation: It proves light is transverse.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE waves and optics: wave motion, sound, stationary waves, Doppler effect, mirrors, lenses, interference, diffraction, and polarization.
front: What is Brewster's law?
back: Brewster's law states that refractive index of a medium equals tangent of polarizing angle.
explanation: At polarizing angle, reflected and refracted rays are perpendicular.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE waves and optics: wave motion, sound, stationary waves, Doppler effect, mirrors, lenses, interference, diffraction, and polarization.
front: Why is sound in air longitudinal?
back: In air, particles vibrate parallel to direction of wave propagation, so sound is longitudinal.
explanation: It travels as compressions and rarefactions.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE waves and optics: wave motion, sound, stationary waves, Doppler effect, mirrors, lenses, interference, diffraction, and polarization.
front: What is pressure amplitude in sound?
back: Pressure amplitude is maximum change in pressure from normal pressure during propagation of a sound wave.
explanation: It is related to intensity of sound.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE waves and optics: wave motion, sound, stationary waves, Doppler effect, mirrors, lenses, interference, diffraction, and polarization.
front: Which harmonics are present in an open pipe?
back: An open pipe supports all harmonics: first, second, third, and so on.
explanation: Both ends are displacement antinodes.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE waves and optics: wave motion, sound, stationary waves, Doppler effect, mirrors, lenses, interference, diffraction, and polarization.
front: What are the boundary conditions in a pipe closed at one end?
back: Closed end is displacement node and open end is displacement antinode.
explanation: Only odd harmonics are present.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE waves and optics: wave motion, sound, stationary waves, Doppler effect, mirrors, lenses, interference, diffraction, and polarization.
front: What does mirror formula relate?
back: Mirror formula relates focal length, object distance, and image distance for spherical mirrors.
explanation: Use sign convention carefully in numerical problems.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE waves and optics: wave motion, sound, stationary waves, Doppler effect, mirrors, lenses, interference, diffraction, and polarization.
front: What is power of a lens?
back: Power of a lens is reciprocal of focal length in meters.
explanation: Its unit is dioptre.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE waves and optics: wave motion, sound, stationary waves, Doppler effect, mirrors, lenses, interference, diffraction, and polarization.
front: What is total internal reflection?
back: Total internal reflection is complete reflection of light back into denser medium when angle of incidence exceeds critical angle.
explanation: It occurs only from denser to rarer medium.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE waves and optics: wave motion, sound, stationary waves, Doppler effect, mirrors, lenses, interference, diffraction, and polarization.
front: What is critical angle?
back: Critical angle is angle of incidence in denser medium for which angle of refraction in rarer medium is 90 degrees.
explanation: Beyond it, total internal reflection occurs.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE waves and optics: wave motion, sound, stationary waves, Doppler effect, mirrors, lenses, interference, diffraction, and polarization.
front: What principle is used in optical fibers?
back: Optical fibers work on total internal reflection.
explanation: They are used in communication and medical endoscopy.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE waves and optics: wave motion, sound, stationary waves, Doppler effect, mirrors, lenses, interference, diffraction, and polarization.
front: What are beats?
back: Beats are periodic variations in loudness produced by superposition of two sound waves of slightly different frequencies.
explanation: Beat frequency equals difference between the two frequencies.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE waves and optics: wave motion, sound, stationary waves, Doppler effect, mirrors, lenses, interference, diffraction, and polarization.
front: What is resonance?
back: Resonance occurs when a system vibrates with maximum amplitude due to driving frequency equal to natural frequency.
explanation: It is important in sound columns and oscillations.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE waves and optics: wave motion, sound, stationary waves, Doppler effect, mirrors, lenses, interference, diffraction, and polarization.
front: How do interference and diffraction differ?
back: Interference is superposition from different coherent sources, while diffraction is superposition from different parts of the same wavefront.
explanation: Both show wave nature of light.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE waves and optics: wave motion, sound, stationary waves, Doppler effect, mirrors, lenses, interference, diffraction, and polarization.
front: What are polarizer and analyzer?
back: A polarizer produces plane polarized light, while an analyzer tests or detects polarization.
explanation: They are used in polarization experiments.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE waves and optics: wave motion, sound, stationary waves, Doppler effect, mirrors, lenses, interference, diffraction, and polarization.
front: What does Malus law state?
back: Intensity transmitted through analyzer varies as square of cosine of angle between transmission axes.
explanation: It applies to plane polarized light.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE waves and optics: wave motion, sound, stationary waves, Doppler effect, mirrors, lenses, interference, diffraction, and polarization.
front: Name applications of Doppler effect.
back: Applications include radar speed detection, astronomy redshift, ultrasound blood flow measurement, and siren frequency change.
explanation: It links frequency shift with relative motion.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE waves and optics: wave motion, sound, stationary waves, Doppler effect, mirrors, lenses, interference, diffraction, and polarization.
front: Which color deviates most in a prism and why?
back: Violet deviates most and red least because refractive index is greater for shorter wavelength.
explanation: This causes dispersion of white light.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE waves and optics: wave motion, sound, stationary waves, Doppler effect, mirrors, lenses, interference, diffraction, and polarization.
front: What is spherical aberration?
back: Spherical aberration is image defect due to marginal and paraxial rays focusing at different points in a spherical lens or mirror.
explanation: It can be reduced by using stops or parabolic surfaces.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE waves and optics: wave motion, sound, stationary waves, Doppler effect, mirrors, lenses, interference, diffraction, and polarization.
front: What is the relation between wave speed, frequency, and wavelength?
back: Wave speed equals frequency multiplied by wavelength.
explanation: This relation applies to all waves.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE waves and optics: wave motion, sound, stationary waves, Doppler effect, mirrors, lenses, interference, diffraction, and polarization.
front: What is the fastest CEE method to revise waves and optics?
back: Revise wave definitions, pipe-string harmonics, sound qualities, mirror-lens sign rules, and interference-diffraction-polarization differences.
explanation: CEE often asks conditions, graphs, fringe concepts, Doppler logic, and optical instrument principles.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE: electric circuits, AC, magnetism, magnetic materials, induction, transformer, and semiconductor applications.
front: What is electrical resistance?
back: Resistance is opposition offered by a conductor to flow of electric current.
explanation: Its SI unit is ohm.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE: electric circuits, AC, magnetism, magnetic materials, induction, transformer, and semiconductor applications.
front: How do EMF and potential difference differ?
back: EMF is energy supplied per unit charge by a source, while potential difference is energy used per unit charge between two points.
explanation: EMF exists even when circuit is open.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE: electric circuits, AC, magnetism, magnetic materials, induction, transformer, and semiconductor applications.
front: What is Ohm's law?
back: Current through a conductor is directly proportional to potential difference across it if temperature and physical conditions remain constant.
explanation: V = IR.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE: electric circuits, AC, magnetism, magnetic materials, induction, transformer, and semiconductor applications.
front: What is Joule's law of heating?
back: Heat produced in a conductor is proportional to square of current, resistance, and time.
explanation: It explains heating effect of current.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE: electric circuits, AC, magnetism, magnetic materials, induction, transformer, and semiconductor applications.
front: What is electrical power?
back: Electrical power is rate at which electrical energy is consumed or converted.
explanation: P = VI = I²R = V²/R.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE: electric circuits, AC, magnetism, magnetic materials, induction, transformer, and semiconductor applications.
front: What is Kirchhoff's current law?
back: Total current entering a junction equals total current leaving the junction.
explanation: It is also called junction rule.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE: electric circuits, AC, magnetism, magnetic materials, induction, transformer, and semiconductor applications.
front: What is Kirchhoff's voltage law?
back: The algebraic sum of potential changes around any closed loop is zero.
explanation: It is also called loop rule.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE: electric circuits, AC, magnetism, magnetic materials, induction, transformer, and semiconductor applications.
front: What happens to equivalent resistance in series combination?
back: In series, equivalent resistance is sum of individual resistances.
explanation: Same current flows through all resistors.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE: electric circuits, AC, magnetism, magnetic materials, induction, transformer, and semiconductor applications.
front: What happens to equivalent resistance in parallel combination?
back: In parallel, reciprocal of equivalent resistance equals sum of reciprocals of individual resistances.
explanation: Same potential difference exists across each resistor.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE: electric circuits, AC, magnetism, magnetic materials, induction, transformer, and semiconductor applications.
front: What is the balanced condition of Wheatstone bridge?
back: In a balanced Wheatstone bridge, ratio of two resistances in one arm equals ratio of two resistances in the other arm.
explanation: It is used to measure unknown resistance.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE: electric circuits, AC, magnetism, magnetic materials, induction, transformer, and semiconductor applications.
front: What is the principle of meter bridge?
back: Meter bridge works on Wheatstone bridge principle using a one-meter uniform resistance wire.
explanation: It is used to find unknown resistance.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE: electric circuits, AC, magnetism, magnetic materials, induction, transformer, and semiconductor applications.
front: What is the principle of potentiometer?
back: Potential drop along a uniform wire is directly proportional to its length when steady current flows.
explanation: It measures EMF or potential difference without drawing current at balance.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE: electric circuits, AC, magnetism, magnetic materials, induction, transformer, and semiconductor applications.
front: How is a galvanometer converted into an ammeter?
back: A galvanometer is converted into an ammeter by connecting a low resistance shunt in parallel.
explanation: This allows measurement of large current.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE: electric circuits, AC, magnetism, magnetic materials, induction, transformer, and semiconductor applications.
front: How is a galvanometer converted into a voltmeter?
back: A galvanometer is converted into a voltmeter by connecting a high resistance in series.
explanation: This limits current through the galvanometer.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE: electric circuits, AC, magnetism, magnetic materials, induction, transformer, and semiconductor applications.
front: What is Seebeck effect?
back: Seebeck effect is production of EMF in a thermocouple when its two junctions are at different temperatures.
explanation: It is used in thermocouples.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE: electric circuits, AC, magnetism, magnetic materials, induction, transformer, and semiconductor applications.
front: What is Peltier effect?
back: Peltier effect is heating or cooling at a junction of two different conductors when current passes through it.
explanation: It is reverse of Seebeck effect.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE: electric circuits, AC, magnetism, magnetic materials, induction, transformer, and semiconductor applications.
front: What is a thermocouple?
back: A thermocouple is a pair of dissimilar metals joined to form two junctions, producing EMF when junctions are at different temperatures.
explanation: It works on Seebeck effect.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE: electric circuits, AC, magnetism, magnetic materials, induction, transformer, and semiconductor applications.
front: What is alternating current?
back: Alternating current is current whose magnitude and direction change periodically with time.
explanation: Household supply is AC.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE: electric circuits, AC, magnetism, magnetic materials, induction, transformer, and semiconductor applications.
front: What is RMS value of AC?
back: RMS value of AC is the equivalent DC value that produces the same heating effect in a resistor.
explanation: For sinusoidal AC, Irms = I0 divided by square root of 2.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE: electric circuits, AC, magnetism, magnetic materials, induction, transformer, and semiconductor applications.
front: What is impedance?
back: Impedance is total opposition offered by an AC circuit to alternating current.
explanation: It includes resistance and reactance.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE: electric circuits, AC, magnetism, magnetic materials, induction, transformer, and semiconductor applications.
front: What is resonance in an LCR circuit?
back: Resonance occurs when inductive reactance equals capacitive reactance, making impedance minimum in series LCR.
explanation: Current becomes maximum at resonance.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE: electric circuits, AC, magnetism, magnetic materials, induction, transformer, and semiconductor applications.
front: What is Q-factor in an LCR circuit?
back: Q-factor measures sharpness of resonance and energy selectivity of the circuit.
explanation: Higher Q means sharper resonance.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE: electric circuits, AC, magnetism, magnetic materials, induction, transformer, and semiconductor applications.
front: What is the function of a diode bridge rectifier?
back: A diode bridge rectifier converts AC into pulsating DC using four diodes.
explanation: It provides full-wave rectification.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE: electric circuits, AC, magnetism, magnetic materials, induction, transformer, and semiconductor applications.
front: What are magnetic domains?
back: Magnetic domains are small regions in ferromagnetic materials where atomic magnetic moments are aligned in the same direction.
explanation: Magnetization occurs when domains align.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE: electric circuits, AC, magnetism, magnetic materials, induction, transformer, and semiconductor applications.
front: What are diamagnetic materials?
back: Diamagnetic materials are weakly repelled by magnetic fields and have negative susceptibility.
explanation: Examples include copper, bismuth, and water.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE: electric circuits, AC, magnetism, magnetic materials, induction, transformer, and semiconductor applications.
front: What are paramagnetic materials?
back: Paramagnetic materials are weakly attracted by magnetic fields and have small positive susceptibility.
explanation: Examples include aluminium and oxygen.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE: electric circuits, AC, magnetism, magnetic materials, induction, transformer, and semiconductor applications.
front: What are ferromagnetic materials?
back: Ferromagnetic materials are strongly attracted by magnetic fields and can retain magnetization.
explanation: Iron, cobalt, and nickel are examples.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE: electric circuits, AC, magnetism, magnetic materials, induction, transformer, and semiconductor applications.
front: What is magnetic hysteresis?
back: Hysteresis is lagging of magnetization behind magnetizing field during cyclic magnetization.
explanation: Hysteresis loop area represents energy loss per cycle.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE: electric circuits, AC, magnetism, magnetic materials, induction, transformer, and semiconductor applications.
front: What is the direction of magnetic field around a straight current-carrying conductor?
back: Direction is given by right-hand thumb rule: thumb along current, curled fingers show magnetic field direction.
explanation: Field lines are concentric circles around the wire.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE: electric circuits, AC, magnetism, magnetic materials, induction, transformer, and semiconductor applications.
front: What happens to magnetic field at center of circular coil when number of turns increases?
back: Magnetic field at center increases directly with number of turns.
explanation: It also depends on current and radius.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE: electric circuits, AC, magnetism, magnetic materials, induction, transformer, and semiconductor applications.
front: What is magnetic field inside a long solenoid like?
back: Magnetic field inside a long solenoid is strong, nearly uniform, and along the axis.
explanation: A solenoid behaves like a bar magnet.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE: electric circuits, AC, magnetism, magnetic materials, induction, transformer, and semiconductor applications.
front: What force acts on a moving charge in a magnetic field?
back: A moving charge experiences magnetic force perpendicular to both velocity and magnetic field.
explanation: Force is maximum when velocity is perpendicular to magnetic field.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE: electric circuits, AC, magnetism, magnetic materials, induction, transformer, and semiconductor applications.
front: What happens to a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field?
back: It experiences a force if current direction is not parallel to magnetic field.
explanation: Direction is given by Fleming's left-hand rule.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE: electric circuits, AC, magnetism, magnetic materials, induction, transformer, and semiconductor applications.
front: What is Hall effect?
back: Hall effect is development of transverse voltage across a current-carrying conductor or semiconductor placed in magnetic field.
explanation: It helps determine type and density of charge carriers.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE: electric circuits, AC, magnetism, magnetic materials, induction, transformer, and semiconductor applications.
front: What is Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction?
back: Induced EMF in a circuit is proportional to rate of change of magnetic flux linked with the circuit.
explanation: It is the principle of generators and transformers.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE: electric circuits, AC, magnetism, magnetic materials, induction, transformer, and semiconductor applications.
front: What is Lenz's law?
back: Induced current flows in such a direction that it opposes the change producing it.
explanation: It follows conservation of energy.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE: electric circuits, AC, magnetism, magnetic materials, induction, transformer, and semiconductor applications.
front: What is the principle of AC generator?
back: An AC generator works on electromagnetic induction by rotating a coil in a magnetic field.
explanation: Induced EMF changes direction periodically.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE: electric circuits, AC, magnetism, magnetic materials, induction, transformer, and semiconductor applications.
front: What is the principle of transformer?
back: A transformer works on mutual induction between two coils wound on a common core.
explanation: It changes AC voltage, not DC voltage.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE: electric circuits, AC, magnetism, magnetic materials, induction, transformer, and semiconductor applications.
front: What is a step-up transformer?
back: A step-up transformer increases AC voltage and has more turns in secondary coil than primary coil.
explanation: Current decreases ideally when voltage increases.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE: electric circuits, AC, magnetism, magnetic materials, induction, transformer, and semiconductor applications.
front: What is a step-down transformer?
back: A step-down transformer decreases AC voltage and has fewer turns in secondary coil than primary coil.
explanation: It is used in chargers and power distribution.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE: electric circuits, AC, magnetism, magnetic materials, induction, transformer, and semiconductor applications.
front: What are eddy currents?
back: Eddy currents are circulating currents induced in bulk conductors due to changing magnetic flux.
explanation: They can cause heating and energy loss.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE: electric circuits, AC, magnetism, magnetic materials, induction, transformer, and semiconductor applications.
front: What is self-inductance?
back: Self-inductance is the property of a coil by which change in its own current induces EMF in itself.
explanation: Its SI unit is henry.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE: electric circuits, AC, magnetism, magnetic materials, induction, transformer, and semiconductor applications.
front: What is mutual inductance?
back: Mutual inductance is the property by which change in current in one coil induces EMF in a nearby coil.
explanation: It is the basis of transformer action.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE: electric circuits, AC, magnetism, magnetic materials, induction, transformer, and semiconductor applications.
front: Where is energy stored in an inductor?
back: Energy in an inductor is stored in its magnetic field.
explanation: Energy stored equals 1/2 LI².

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE: electric circuits, AC, magnetism, magnetic materials, induction, transformer, and semiconductor applications.
front: What is power factor in AC circuit?
back: Power factor is cosine of phase angle between voltage and current.
explanation: It determines real power consumed in AC circuits.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE: electric circuits, AC, magnetism, magnetic materials, induction, transformer, and semiconductor applications.
front: How do voltage and current phase differ in pure resistor, inductor, and capacitor?
back: In resistor they are in phase, in inductor current lags voltage, and in capacitor current leads voltage.
hint: R in phase, L lag, C lead.
explanation: This is a common AC concept trap.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE: electric circuits, AC, magnetism, magnetic materials, induction, transformer, and semiconductor applications.
front: What is relative permeability?
back: Relative permeability is ratio of permeability of a material to permeability of free space.
explanation: It shows how easily a material supports magnetic field.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE: electric circuits, AC, magnetism, magnetic materials, induction, transformer, and semiconductor applications.
front: What is magnetic susceptibility?
back: Magnetic susceptibility measures how much a material becomes magnetized in an applied magnetic field.
explanation: It is negative for diamagnetic substances and positive for paramagnetic substances.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE: electric circuits, AC, magnetism, magnetic materials, induction, transformer, and semiconductor applications.
front: How are eddy current losses reduced in transformers?
back: Eddy current losses are reduced by using laminated iron cores.
explanation: Lamination increases resistance to circulating currents.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE: electric circuits, AC, magnetism, magnetic materials, induction, transformer, and semiconductor applications.
front: What is the fastest CEE method to revise current electricity and magnetism?
back: Revise circuit laws, bridge principles, AC phase relations, magnetic material behavior, field rules, and induction devices.
explanation: CEE often asks conversion of galvanometer, LCR resonance, transformer principles, and direction rules.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE electrostatics: charge, Coulomb law, electric field, potential, Gauss law, capacitors, dielectrics, and energy density.
front: What is electric charge?
back: Electric charge is a fundamental property of matter responsible for electric force and interaction.
explanation: Charge is conserved and quantized.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE electrostatics: charge, Coulomb law, electric field, potential, Gauss law, capacitors, dielectrics, and energy density.
front: What does quantization of charge mean?
back: Quantization means charge exists as integral multiples of elementary charge e.
explanation: Charge cannot have arbitrary fractional values in ordinary isolated bodies.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE electrostatics: charge, Coulomb law, electric field, potential, Gauss law, capacitors, dielectrics, and energy density.
front: What does conservation of charge mean?
back: Total electric charge of an isolated system remains constant.
hint: Charge is not created or destroyed.
explanation: Charges can only transfer from one body to another.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE electrostatics: charge, Coulomb law, electric field, potential, Gauss law, capacitors, dielectrics, and energy density.
front: What is electrostatic induction?
back: Electrostatic induction is redistribution of charges in a body due to nearby charged body without contact.
explanation: It can be used to charge conductors.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE electrostatics: charge, Coulomb law, electric field, potential, Gauss law, capacitors, dielectrics, and energy density.
front: What is Coulomb's law?
back: Electrostatic force between two point charges is directly proportional to product of charges and inversely proportional to square of distance between them.
explanation: Like charges repel and unlike charges attract.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE electrostatics: charge, Coulomb law, electric field, potential, Gauss law, capacitors, dielectrics, and energy density.
front: How does medium affect electrostatic force?
back: Electrostatic force decreases in a medium with higher dielectric constant compared with vacuum.
explanation: Force is inversely proportional to dielectric constant.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE electrostatics: charge, Coulomb law, electric field, potential, Gauss law, capacitors, dielectrics, and energy density.
front: What is electric field strength?
back: Electric field strength is force experienced per unit positive test charge at a point.
explanation: Its unit is N/C or V/m.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE electrostatics: charge, Coulomb law, electric field, potential, Gauss law, capacitors, dielectrics, and energy density.
front: What is the direction of electric field?
back: Electric field direction is the direction of force on a positive test charge.
explanation: Field lines emerge from positive charge and end on negative charge.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE electrostatics: charge, Coulomb law, electric field, potential, Gauss law, capacitors, dielectrics, and energy density.
front: What do electric field lines represent?
back: Electric field lines show direction and relative strength of electric field.
explanation: Field lines never intersect.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE electrostatics: charge, Coulomb law, electric field, potential, Gauss law, capacitors, dielectrics, and energy density.
front: What is electric potential?
back: Electric potential at a point is work done per unit positive charge in bringing it from infinity to that point.
explanation: Its SI unit is volt.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE electrostatics: charge, Coulomb law, electric field, potential, Gauss law, capacitors, dielectrics, and energy density.
front: What is electric potential energy?
back: Electric potential energy is energy possessed by a charge due to its position in an electric field.
explanation: It depends on charge, field, and position.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE electrostatics: charge, Coulomb law, electric field, potential, Gauss law, capacitors, dielectrics, and energy density.
front: How are electric field and potential related?
back: Electric field is negative gradient of electric potential.
explanation: In uniform field, E = V/d.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE electrostatics: charge, Coulomb law, electric field, potential, Gauss law, capacitors, dielectrics, and energy density.
front: What is electric flux?
back: Electric flux is the measure of electric field passing through a surface.
explanation: It depends on electric field, area, and angle.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE electrostatics: charge, Coulomb law, electric field, potential, Gauss law, capacitors, dielectrics, and energy density.
front: What is Gauss's law?
back: Total electric flux through a closed surface equals enclosed charge divided by permittivity of free space.
hint: Flux equals charge over epsilon zero.
explanation: It is useful for symmetric charge distributions.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE electrostatics: charge, Coulomb law, electric field, potential, Gauss law, capacitors, dielectrics, and energy density.
front: What is a Gaussian surface?
back: A Gaussian surface is an imaginary closed surface used to apply Gauss's law.
explanation: It is chosen according to symmetry of charge distribution.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE electrostatics: charge, Coulomb law, electric field, potential, Gauss law, capacitors, dielectrics, and energy density.
front: What does slope of electric potential-distance graph represent?
back: Negative slope of potential-distance graph represents electric field.
explanation: Steeper potential graph means stronger electric field.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE electrostatics: charge, Coulomb law, electric field, potential, Gauss law, capacitors, dielectrics, and energy density.
front: What is electric field inside a conductor in electrostatic equilibrium?
back: Electric field inside a conductor is zero in electrostatic equilibrium.
explanation: Excess charge resides on the outer surface.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE electrostatics: charge, Coulomb law, electric field, potential, Gauss law, capacitors, dielectrics, and energy density.
front: What is an equipotential surface?
back: An equipotential surface has same electric potential at every point.
explanation: No work is done moving charge along it.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE electrostatics: charge, Coulomb law, electric field, potential, Gauss law, capacitors, dielectrics, and energy density.
front: What is a capacitor?
back: A capacitor is a device that stores electric charge and electrical energy.
explanation: It usually consists of two conductors separated by an insulator.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE electrostatics: charge, Coulomb law, electric field, potential, Gauss law, capacitors, dielectrics, and energy density.
front: What is capacitance?
back: Capacitance is charge stored per unit potential difference.
explanation: Its SI unit is farad.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE electrostatics: charge, Coulomb law, electric field, potential, Gauss law, capacitors, dielectrics, and energy density.
front: On what factors does capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor depend?
back: It depends directly on plate area and dielectric constant, and inversely on separation between plates.
explanation: C = epsilon A/d.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE electrostatics: charge, Coulomb law, electric field, potential, Gauss law, capacitors, dielectrics, and energy density.
front: What happens to equivalent capacitance in series combination?
back: In series, reciprocal of equivalent capacitance equals sum of reciprocals of individual capacitances.
explanation: Same charge appears on each capacitor.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE electrostatics: charge, Coulomb law, electric field, potential, Gauss law, capacitors, dielectrics, and energy density.
front: What happens to equivalent capacitance in parallel combination?
back: In parallel, equivalent capacitance is sum of individual capacitances.
explanation: Same voltage exists across each capacitor.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE electrostatics: charge, Coulomb law, electric field, potential, Gauss law, capacitors, dielectrics, and energy density.
front: Where is energy stored in a charged capacitor?
back: Energy is stored in the electric field between capacitor plates.
explanation: Energy can be written as 1/2 CV².

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE electrostatics: charge, Coulomb law, electric field, potential, Gauss law, capacitors, dielectrics, and energy density.
front: What is energy density in an electric field?
back: Energy density is energy stored per unit volume in an electric field.
explanation: For vacuum, it is proportional to E squared.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE electrostatics: charge, Coulomb law, electric field, potential, Gauss law, capacitors, dielectrics, and energy density.
front: What is a dielectric?
back: A dielectric is an insulating material that can be polarized in an electric field.
explanation: It increases capacitance when inserted between capacitor plates.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE electrostatics: charge, Coulomb law, electric field, potential, Gauss law, capacitors, dielectrics, and energy density.
front: What happens when dielectric is inserted into an isolated charged capacitor?
back: Capacitance increases, potential difference decreases, and stored energy decreases.
explanation: The dielectric reduces effective electric field.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE electrostatics: charge, Coulomb law, electric field, potential, Gauss law, capacitors, dielectrics, and energy density.
front: What is an electric dipole?
back: An electric dipole consists of two equal and opposite charges separated by a small distance.
explanation: It has dipole moment directed from negative to positive charge.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE electrostatics: charge, Coulomb law, electric field, potential, Gauss law, capacitors, dielectrics, and energy density.
front: What is electric dipole moment?
back: Electric dipole moment is product of charge and separation between charges, directed from negative to positive charge.
explanation: It is a vector quantity.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE electrostatics: charge, Coulomb law, electric field, potential, Gauss law, capacitors, dielectrics, and energy density.
front: What is principle of superposition in electrostatics?
back: Net force or field due to multiple charges is vector sum of forces or fields due to individual charges.
explanation: It is essential in multi-charge problems.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE electrostatics: charge, Coulomb law, electric field, potential, Gauss law, capacitors, dielectrics, and energy density.
front: How does electric potential due to a point charge vary with distance?
back: Electric potential due to a point charge varies inversely with distance from the charge.
explanation: Potential is scalar.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE electrostatics: charge, Coulomb law, electric field, potential, Gauss law, capacitors, dielectrics, and energy density.
front: How does electric field due to a point charge vary with distance?
back: Electric field due to a point charge varies inversely with square of distance.
explanation: It is radial outward for positive charge and inward for negative charge.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE electrostatics: charge, Coulomb law, electric field, potential, Gauss law, capacitors, dielectrics, and energy density.
front: Can electric field be zero where electric potential is non-zero?
back: Yes, electric field can be zero at a point where potential is non-zero.
explanation: Potential value and field strength are different concepts.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE electrostatics: charge, Coulomb law, electric field, potential, Gauss law, capacitors, dielectrics, and energy density.
front: What is electrostatic shielding?
back: Electrostatic shielding is protection of a region from external electric fields using a conductor.
explanation: Electric field inside a closed conductor is zero.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE electrostatics: charge, Coulomb law, electric field, potential, Gauss law, capacitors, dielectrics, and energy density.
front: What is the principle of a capacitor?
back: A capacitor stores large charge at small potential difference using electrostatic induction between two conductors.
explanation: Opposite charges appear on facing plates.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE electrostatics: charge, Coulomb law, electric field, potential, Gauss law, capacitors, dielectrics, and energy density.
front: Name common uses of capacitors.
back: Capacitors are used in energy storage, filtering, tuning circuits, camera flash, and smoothing rectified current.
explanation: They can charge and discharge rapidly.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE electrostatics: charge, Coulomb law, electric field, potential, Gauss law, capacitors, dielectrics, and energy density.
front: Why do electric field lines never cross?
back: If field lines crossed, electric field would have two directions at one point, which is impossible.
hint: One field direction at a point.
explanation: This is a common conceptual MCQ.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE electrostatics: charge, Coulomb law, electric field, potential, Gauss law, capacitors, dielectrics, and energy density.
front: What is potential difference?
back: Potential difference between two points is work done per unit charge in moving charge between them.
explanation: It drives current in a circuit.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE electrostatics: charge, Coulomb law, electric field, potential, Gauss law, capacitors, dielectrics, and energy density.
front: How do like and unlike charges interact?
back: Like charges repel, while unlike charges attract.
explanation: This follows from Coulomb's law sign convention.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE electrostatics: charge, Coulomb law, electric field, potential, Gauss law, capacitors, dielectrics, and energy density.
front: Where does excess charge reside on a conductor in electrostatic equilibrium?
back: Excess charge resides on the outer surface of a conductor.
explanation: This occurs because charges repel each other.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE electrostatics: charge, Coulomb law, electric field, potential, Gauss law, capacitors, dielectrics, and energy density.
front: What remains same for capacitors connected in series?
back: Charge on each capacitor is same in series combination.
explanation: Voltage divides among capacitors.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE electrostatics: charge, Coulomb law, electric field, potential, Gauss law, capacitors, dielectrics, and energy density.
front: What remains same for capacitors connected in parallel?
back: Potential difference across each capacitor is same in parallel combination.
explanation: Charges divide according to capacitance.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE electrostatics: charge, Coulomb law, electric field, potential, Gauss law, capacitors, dielectrics, and energy density.
front: What is polarization of dielectric?
back: Polarization is separation or alignment of positive and negative charges inside dielectric under electric field.
explanation: It reduces net electric field inside dielectric.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE electrostatics: charge, Coulomb law, electric field, potential, Gauss law, capacitors, dielectrics, and energy density.
front: How does electric field graph vary for a point charge?
back: Electric field decreases with square of distance from point charge.
explanation: It is very strong near the charge and weak far away.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE electrostatics: charge, Coulomb law, electric field, potential, Gauss law, capacitors, dielectrics, and energy density.
front: How does potential graph vary for a point charge?
back: Electric potential decreases inversely with distance from point charge.
explanation: Potential is positive for positive charge and negative for negative charge.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE electrostatics: charge, Coulomb law, electric field, potential, Gauss law, capacitors, dielectrics, and energy density.
front: When is electric flux through a surface zero?
back: Flux is zero when electric field is parallel to the surface or when net enclosed charge is zero for a closed surface.
explanation: Flux depends on E cos theta.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE electrostatics: charge, Coulomb law, electric field, potential, Gauss law, capacitors, dielectrics, and energy density.
front: How does a lightning conductor protect buildings?
back: A lightning conductor provides a low-resistance path for charge to flow safely to Earth.
explanation: It reduces damage from lightning strikes.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE electrostatics: charge, Coulomb law, electric field, potential, Gauss law, capacitors, dielectrics, and energy density.
front: What is a uniform electric field?
back: A uniform electric field has same magnitude and direction at every point in a region.
explanation: Field between large parallel plates is approximately uniform.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE electrostatics: charge, Coulomb law, electric field, potential, Gauss law, capacitors, dielectrics, and energy density.
front: How does plate area and separation affect capacitance?
back: Capacitance increases with plate area and decreases with plate separation.
explanation: This is key for parallel plate capacitor questions.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE electrostatics: charge, Coulomb law, electric field, potential, Gauss law, capacitors, dielectrics, and energy density.
front: What is the fastest CEE method to revise electrostatics and capacitors?
back: Revise charge laws, field-potential relation, Gauss law symmetry, conductor properties, capacitor combinations, and dielectric effects.
explanation: CEE often asks inverse-square relations, graph meanings, series-parallel capacitor logic, and dielectric changes.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE modern physics: nucleus, radioactivity, photoelectric effect, Bohr theory, X-rays, semiconductors, logic gates, and recent physics trends.
front: What is the nucleus of an atom?
back: The nucleus is the small dense positively charged central part of an atom containing protons and neutrons.
explanation: Nearly all atomic mass is in the nucleus.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE modern physics: nucleus, radioactivity, photoelectric effect, Bohr theory, X-rays, semiconductors, logic gates, and recent physics trends.
front: What determines nuclear charge?
back: Nuclear charge is determined by number of protons and equals +Ze.
explanation: Neutrons do not contribute to charge.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE modern physics: nucleus, radioactivity, photoelectric effect, Bohr theory, X-rays, semiconductors, logic gates, and recent physics trends.
front: How does nuclear radius depend on mass number?
back: Nuclear radius is proportional to cube root of mass number.
explanation: Nuclear volume is proportional to mass number.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE modern physics: nucleus, radioactivity, photoelectric effect, Bohr theory, X-rays, semiconductors, logic gates, and recent physics trends.
front: Why is nuclear density nearly constant?
back: Nuclear mass and nuclear volume both increase approximately proportional to mass number.
explanation: This makes nuclear density almost independent of nucleus size.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE modern physics: nucleus, radioactivity, photoelectric effect, Bohr theory, X-rays, semiconductors, logic gates, and recent physics trends.
front: What is mass defect?
back: Mass defect is difference between total mass of separate nucleons and actual mass of nucleus.
explanation: It appears as binding energy.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE modern physics: nucleus, radioactivity, photoelectric effect, Bohr theory, X-rays, semiconductors, logic gates, and recent physics trends.
front: What is binding energy?
back: Binding energy is energy required to separate a nucleus completely into its nucleons.
explanation: Greater binding energy per nucleon means greater stability.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE modern physics: nucleus, radioactivity, photoelectric effect, Bohr theory, X-rays, semiconductors, logic gates, and recent physics trends.
front: What is Einstein's mass-energy relation?
back: Einstein's relation is E = mc², showing mass and energy are equivalent.
explanation: It explains energy release in nuclear reactions.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE modern physics: nucleus, radioactivity, photoelectric effect, Bohr theory, X-rays, semiconductors, logic gates, and recent physics trends.
front: What is nuclear fusion?
back: Nuclear fusion is combining of light nuclei to form a heavier nucleus with release of energy.
explanation: Fusion powers the Sun and stars.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE modern physics: nucleus, radioactivity, photoelectric effect, Bohr theory, X-rays, semiconductors, logic gates, and recent physics trends.
front: What is nuclear fission?
back: Nuclear fission is splitting of a heavy nucleus into lighter nuclei with release of energy and neutrons.
explanation: It is used in nuclear reactors.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE modern physics: nucleus, radioactivity, photoelectric effect, Bohr theory, X-rays, semiconductors, logic gates, and recent physics trends.
front: How does an electron move in a uniform electric field?
back: An electron experiences force opposite to electric field direction and accelerates due to its charge.
explanation: Force on charge is qE.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE modern physics: nucleus, radioactivity, photoelectric effect, Bohr theory, X-rays, semiconductors, logic gates, and recent physics trends.
front: How does an electron move in a magnetic field perpendicular to velocity?
back: It moves in a circular path because magnetic force acts perpendicular to velocity.
explanation: Magnetic force provides centripetal force.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE modern physics: nucleus, radioactivity, photoelectric effect, Bohr theory, X-rays, semiconductors, logic gates, and recent physics trends.
front: What did Millikan's oil drop experiment determine?
back: Millikan's oil drop experiment determined the elementary charge of electron.
explanation: It showed charge is quantized.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE modern physics: nucleus, radioactivity, photoelectric effect, Bohr theory, X-rays, semiconductors, logic gates, and recent physics trends.
front: What did J. J. Thomson's experiment determine?
back: J. J. Thomson measured charge-to-mass ratio of electron using cathode rays.
explanation: It helped identify electron as a subatomic particle.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE modern physics: nucleus, radioactivity, photoelectric effect, Bohr theory, X-rays, semiconductors, logic gates, and recent physics trends.
front: What is a photon?
back: A photon is a quantum or packet of electromagnetic radiation with energy E = hf.
explanation: Photon energy depends on frequency.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE modern physics: nucleus, radioactivity, photoelectric effect, Bohr theory, X-rays, semiconductors, logic gates, and recent physics trends.
front: What is photoelectric effect?
back: Photoelectric effect is emission of electrons from a metal surface when light of suitable frequency falls on it.
explanation: It supports particle nature of light.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE modern physics: nucleus, radioactivity, photoelectric effect, Bohr theory, X-rays, semiconductors, logic gates, and recent physics trends.
front: What is threshold frequency?
back: Threshold frequency is minimum frequency of incident light required to emit photoelectrons from a metal.
explanation: Below it, no emission occurs regardless of intensity.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE modern physics: nucleus, radioactivity, photoelectric effect, Bohr theory, X-rays, semiconductors, logic gates, and recent physics trends.
front: What is work function?
back: Work function is minimum energy required to remove an electron from a metal surface.
explanation: It depends on nature of metal.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE modern physics: nucleus, radioactivity, photoelectric effect, Bohr theory, X-rays, semiconductors, logic gates, and recent physics trends.
front: What is stopping potential?
back: Stopping potential is minimum reverse potential needed to stop the most energetic photoelectrons.
explanation: It measures maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE modern physics: nucleus, radioactivity, photoelectric effect, Bohr theory, X-rays, semiconductors, logic gates, and recent physics trends.
front: What is a key postulate of Bohr's atomic model?
back: Electrons revolve only in certain permitted stationary orbits without radiating energy.
explanation: Radiation occurs during transition between energy levels.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE modern physics: nucleus, radioactivity, photoelectric effect, Bohr theory, X-rays, semiconductors, logic gates, and recent physics trends.
front: What causes spectral lines in hydrogen atom?
back: Spectral lines are produced when electrons transition between quantized energy levels.
explanation: Emission occurs when electron falls to lower energy level.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE modern physics: nucleus, radioactivity, photoelectric effect, Bohr theory, X-rays, semiconductors, logic gates, and recent physics trends.
front: What are energy levels in atoms?
back: Energy levels are fixed allowed energies that electrons can have in an atom.
explanation: Electrons cannot have arbitrary energies in Bohr model.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE modern physics: nucleus, radioactivity, photoelectric effect, Bohr theory, X-rays, semiconductors, logic gates, and recent physics trends.
front: What is de Broglie wavelength?
back: de Broglie wavelength is wavelength associated with a moving particle, equal to h divided by momentum.
explanation: It shows matter waves.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE modern physics: nucleus, radioactivity, photoelectric effect, Bohr theory, X-rays, semiconductors, logic gates, and recent physics trends.
front: What is Heisenberg uncertainty principle?
back: Position and momentum of a particle cannot both be measured simultaneously with unlimited precision.
explanation: It is important for microscopic particles.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE modern physics: nucleus, radioactivity, photoelectric effect, Bohr theory, X-rays, semiconductors, logic gates, and recent physics trends.
front: What are X-rays?
back: X-rays are high-frequency, short-wavelength electromagnetic waves with high penetrating power.
explanation: They are produced when fast electrons strike a heavy target.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE modern physics: nucleus, radioactivity, photoelectric effect, Bohr theory, X-rays, semiconductors, logic gates, and recent physics trends.
front: How are X-rays produced?
back: X-rays are produced when high-speed electrons suddenly decelerate on striking a heavy metal target.
explanation: Tungsten is commonly used as target.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE modern physics: nucleus, radioactivity, photoelectric effect, Bohr theory, X-rays, semiconductors, logic gates, and recent physics trends.
front: Name common uses of X-rays.
back: X-rays are used in medical imaging, cancer therapy, crystallography, security scanning, and industrial defect detection.
explanation: Their penetration makes them useful but hazardous.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE modern physics: nucleus, radioactivity, photoelectric effect, Bohr theory, X-rays, semiconductors, logic gates, and recent physics trends.
front: What is Bragg's law?
back: Bragg's law gives condition for constructive reflection of X-rays from crystal planes: 2d sin theta equals n lambda.
explanation: It is used to study crystal structure.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE modern physics: nucleus, radioactivity, photoelectric effect, Bohr theory, X-rays, semiconductors, logic gates, and recent physics trends.
front: What is radioactivity?
back: Radioactivity is spontaneous disintegration of unstable nuclei with emission of alpha, beta, or gamma radiation.
explanation: It is a nuclear phenomenon.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE modern physics: nucleus, radioactivity, photoelectric effect, Bohr theory, X-rays, semiconductors, logic gates, and recent physics trends.
front: What are alpha rays?
back: Alpha rays are helium nuclei emitted by radioactive substances.
explanation: They have high ionizing power but low penetrating power.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE modern physics: nucleus, radioactivity, photoelectric effect, Bohr theory, X-rays, semiconductors, logic gates, and recent physics trends.
front: What are beta rays?
back: Beta rays are high-speed electrons or positrons emitted during radioactive decay.
explanation: They have moderate ionizing and penetrating power.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE modern physics: nucleus, radioactivity, photoelectric effect, Bohr theory, X-rays, semiconductors, logic gates, and recent physics trends.
front: What are gamma rays?
back: Gamma rays are high-energy electromagnetic radiations emitted from nuclei.
explanation: They have very high penetrating power.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE modern physics: nucleus, radioactivity, photoelectric effect, Bohr theory, X-rays, semiconductors, logic gates, and recent physics trends.
front: What is half-life?
back: Half-life is time required for half of radioactive nuclei in a sample to decay.
explanation: It is constant for a particular isotope.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE modern physics: nucleus, radioactivity, photoelectric effect, Bohr theory, X-rays, semiconductors, logic gates, and recent physics trends.
front: What is mean life?
back: Mean life is average lifetime of radioactive nuclei before decay.
explanation: Mean life is reciprocal of decay constant.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE modern physics: nucleus, radioactivity, photoelectric effect, Bohr theory, X-rays, semiconductors, logic gates, and recent physics trends.
front: How are half-life and mean life related?
back: Half-life equals 0.693 times mean life.
explanation: This relation is frequently tested.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE modern physics: nucleus, radioactivity, photoelectric effect, Bohr theory, X-rays, semiconductors, logic gates, and recent physics trends.
front: What is carbon dating?
back: Carbon dating estimates age of organic remains using decay of radioactive carbon-14.
explanation: It is useful for archaeological and biological samples.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE modern physics: nucleus, radioactivity, photoelectric effect, Bohr theory, X-rays, semiconductors, logic gates, and recent physics trends.
front: Name medical uses of nuclear radiation.
back: Nuclear radiation is used in cancer radiotherapy, diagnosis, imaging, and radioactive tracer studies.
explanation: It must be used with safety precautions.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE modern physics: nucleus, radioactivity, photoelectric effect, Bohr theory, X-rays, semiconductors, logic gates, and recent physics trends.
front: What are health hazards of nuclear radiation?
back: Radiation can damage cells, cause burns, mutations, cancer, infertility, and radiation sickness.
explanation: Protection uses time, distance, and shielding.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE modern physics: nucleus, radioactivity, photoelectric effect, Bohr theory, X-rays, semiconductors, logic gates, and recent physics trends.
front: What are energy bands in solids?
back: Energy bands are ranges of allowed electron energies in solids separated by forbidden energy gaps.
explanation: Band theory explains conductors, semiconductors, and insulators.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE modern physics: nucleus, radioactivity, photoelectric effect, Bohr theory, X-rays, semiconductors, logic gates, and recent physics trends.
front: How do metals, semiconductors, and insulators differ by band gap?
back: Metals have overlapping bands, semiconductors have small band gap, and insulators have large band gap.
explanation: This is the basis of electronic properties.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE modern physics: nucleus, radioactivity, photoelectric effect, Bohr theory, X-rays, semiconductors, logic gates, and recent physics trends.
front: What is an intrinsic semiconductor?
back: An intrinsic semiconductor is a pure semiconductor without intentional impurity doping.
explanation: Electron and hole concentrations are equal.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE modern physics: nucleus, radioactivity, photoelectric effect, Bohr theory, X-rays, semiconductors, logic gates, and recent physics trends.
front: What is an extrinsic semiconductor?
back: An extrinsic semiconductor is a doped semiconductor with increased conductivity.
explanation: It may be n-type or p-type.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE modern physics: nucleus, radioactivity, photoelectric effect, Bohr theory, X-rays, semiconductors, logic gates, and recent physics trends.
front: How do n-type and p-type semiconductors differ?
back: n-type has electrons as majority carriers, while p-type has holes as majority carriers.
explanation: n-type uses pentavalent impurity and p-type uses trivalent impurity.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE modern physics: nucleus, radioactivity, photoelectric effect, Bohr theory, X-rays, semiconductors, logic gates, and recent physics trends.
front: What is a p-n junction diode?
back: A p-n junction diode is formed by joining p-type and n-type semiconductors and allows current mainly in one direction.
explanation: It is used as a rectifier.

subject: Physics

front: How do forward and reverse bias differ in a p-n diode?
back: Forward bias reduces barrier and allows current, while reverse bias increases barrier and nearly stops current.
explanation: Diode conducts mainly in forward bias.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE modern physics: nucleus, radioactivity, photoelectric effect, Bohr theory, X-rays, semiconductors, logic gates, and recent physics trends.
front: How is a p-n diode used as rectifier?
back: A p-n diode converts AC into pulsating DC by allowing current during only one direction of voltage.
explanation: Half-wave and full-wave rectifiers are common.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE modern physics: nucleus, radioactivity, photoelectric effect, Bohr theory, X-rays, semiconductors, logic gates, and recent physics trends.
front: What are logic gates?
back: Logic gates are digital circuits that perform logical operations on binary inputs.
explanation: AND, OR, NOT, NAND, and NOR are common gates.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE modern physics: nucleus, radioactivity, photoelectric effect, Bohr theory, X-rays, semiconductors, logic gates, and recent physics trends.
front: Why are NAND and NOR called universal gates?
back: NAND and NOR are universal because any logic gate can be constructed using only NAND gates or only NOR gates.
explanation: This is a common digital logic concept.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE modern physics: nucleus, radioactivity, photoelectric effect, Bohr theory, X-rays, semiconductors, logic gates, and recent physics trends.
front: What is an antiparticle?
back: An antiparticle has the same mass as its corresponding particle but opposite charge or quantum properties.
explanation: Electron's antiparticle is positron.

subject: Physics
deck_description: High-yield Physics flashcards for CEE modern physics: nucleus, radioactivity, photoelectric effect, Bohr theory, X-rays, semiconductors, logic gates, and recent physics trends.
front: How does Hubble's law support Big Bang theory?
back: Hubble's law shows distant galaxies recede faster, indicating the universe is expanding from an earlier dense state.
explanation: This supports Big Bang cosmology.
