subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for atoms, molecules, valency, formulae, equations, empirical formula, and percentage composition.
front: What is an atom?
back: An atom is the smallest unit of an element that retains the chemical properties of that element.
explanation: Atoms combine to form molecules and compounds.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for atoms, molecules, valency, formulae, equations, empirical formula, and percentage composition.
front: Name the three main subatomic particles of an atom.
back: The three main subatomic particles are proton, neutron, and electron.
explanation: Protons and neutrons are in nucleus; electrons are outside nucleus.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for atoms, molecules, valency, formulae, equations, empirical formula, and percentage composition.
front: What is atomic number?
back: Atomic number is the number of protons present in the nucleus of an atom.
explanation: It determines the identity of an element.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for atoms, molecules, valency, formulae, equations, empirical formula, and percentage composition.
front: What is mass number?
back: Mass number is the total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus of an atom.
explanation: Electrons have negligible mass compared with protons and neutrons.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for atoms, molecules, valency, formulae, equations, empirical formula, and percentage composition.
front: What are isotopes?
back: Isotopes are atoms of the same element having same atomic number but different mass numbers.
explanation: Hydrogen, deuterium, and tritium are isotopes of hydrogen.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for atoms, molecules, valency, formulae, equations, empirical formula, and percentage composition.
front: What is a molecule?
back: A molecule is the smallest particle of a substance that can exist independently and retain its chemical properties.
explanation: Molecules may contain same or different atoms.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for atoms, molecules, valency, formulae, equations, empirical formula, and percentage composition.
front: What is a molecule of an element?
back: A molecule of an element contains atoms of the same element bonded together.
explanation: O2, N2, H2, and Cl2 are examples.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for atoms, molecules, valency, formulae, equations, empirical formula, and percentage composition.
front: What is a molecule of a compound?
back: A molecule of a compound contains atoms of different elements chemically bonded in fixed ratio.
explanation: H2O, CO2, and NH3 are examples.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for atoms, molecules, valency, formulae, equations, empirical formula, and percentage composition.
front: What is valency?
back: Valency is the combining capacity of an atom or radical.
explanation: It depends on number of electrons lost, gained, or shared to complete outer shell.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for atoms, molecules, valency, formulae, equations, empirical formula, and percentage composition.
front: What do monovalent and divalent mean?
back: Monovalent means valency one, while divalent means valency two.
explanation: Na and Cl are monovalent; Mg and O are divalent.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for atoms, molecules, valency, formulae, equations, empirical formula, and percentage composition.
front: What is relative atomic mass?
back: Relative atomic mass is the average mass of atoms of an element compared with one-twelfth mass of carbon-12 atom.
explanation: It has no unit because it is a ratio.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for atoms, molecules, valency, formulae, equations, empirical formula, and percentage composition.
front: What is molecular mass?
back: Molecular mass is the sum of relative atomic masses of all atoms present in a molecule.
explanation: For H2O, molecular mass is 18.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for atoms, molecules, valency, formulae, equations, empirical formula, and percentage composition.
front: What is atomic mass unit?
back: Atomic mass unit is one-twelfth of the mass of one carbon-12 atom.
explanation: It is also called unified atomic mass unit.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for atoms, molecules, valency, formulae, equations, empirical formula, and percentage composition.
front: What is a radical in basic chemistry?
back: A radical is an atom or group of atoms carrying charge and behaving as a single unit in reactions.
explanation: Examples include NH4+, SO4²-, NO3-, and OH-.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for atoms, molecules, valency, formulae, equations, empirical formula, and percentage composition.
front: What are acid radicals and basic radicals?
back: Acid radicals are negative radicals from acids, while basic radicals are positive radicals from bases or salts.
explanation: SO4²- is acid radical; Na+ is basic radical.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for atoms, molecules, valency, formulae, equations, empirical formula, and percentage composition.
front: What is a molecular formula?
back: A molecular formula shows the actual number of atoms of each element in one molecule of a compound.
explanation: Glucose has molecular formula C6H12O6.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for atoms, molecules, valency, formulae, equations, empirical formula, and percentage composition.
front: What is an empirical formula?
back: An empirical formula shows the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms of elements in a compound.
explanation: For glucose, empirical formula is CH2O.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for atoms, molecules, valency, formulae, equations, empirical formula, and percentage composition.
front: How do molecular formula and empirical formula differ?
back: Molecular formula gives actual number of atoms, while empirical formula gives simplest ratio of atoms.
explanation: They may be same for some compounds like H2O.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for atoms, molecules, valency, formulae, equations, empirical formula, and percentage composition.
front: What is a chemical equation?
back: A chemical equation is symbolic representation of a chemical reaction using formulae of reactants and products.
explanation: It must be balanced to obey conservation of mass.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for atoms, molecules, valency, formulae, equations, empirical formula, and percentage composition.
front: What is a balanced chemical equation?
back: A balanced chemical equation has equal number of atoms of each element on both reactant and product sides.
explanation: It follows law of conservation of mass.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for atoms, molecules, valency, formulae, equations, empirical formula, and percentage composition.
front: What do coefficients in a chemical equation represent?
back: Coefficients show relative number of molecules, formula units, or moles involved in a reaction.
explanation: They are used in stoichiometric calculations.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for atoms, molecules, valency, formulae, equations, empirical formula, and percentage composition.
front: How is valency used to write chemical formula?
back: Valencies of combining ions are crossed and simplified to get the formula of a compound.
explanation: For Mg2+ and Cl-, formula becomes MgCl2.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for atoms, molecules, valency, formulae, equations, empirical formula, and percentage composition.
front: What is percentage composition?
back: Percentage composition is the percentage by mass of each element present in a compound.
explanation: It is calculated using atomic masses and molecular mass.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for atoms, molecules, valency, formulae, equations, empirical formula, and percentage composition.
front: How is percentage of an element in a compound calculated?
back: Percentage of element equals total mass of that element in formula divided by molecular mass, multiplied by 100.
explanation: Use atomic masses carefully.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for atoms, molecules, valency, formulae, equations, empirical formula, and percentage composition.
front: What are the steps to find empirical formula from percentage composition?
back: Divide percentages by atomic masses, convert to simplest mole ratio, then write formula.
explanation: Assume 100 g sample if percentages are given.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for atoms, molecules, valency, formulae, equations, empirical formula, and percentage composition.
front: How does an atom differ from an ion?
back: An atom is electrically neutral, while an ion carries positive or negative charge due to loss or gain of electrons.
explanation: Cation is positive; anion is negative.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for atoms, molecules, valency, formulae, equations, empirical formula, and percentage composition.
front: What are cations and anions?
back: Cations are positively charged ions, while anions are negatively charged ions.
explanation: Metals usually form cations; non-metals usually form anions.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for atoms, molecules, valency, formulae, equations, empirical formula, and percentage composition.
front: What is formula mass?
back: Formula mass is the sum of atomic masses of all atoms in the formula unit of an ionic compound.
explanation: It is similar to molecular mass but used for ionic substances.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for atoms, molecules, valency, formulae, equations, empirical formula, and percentage composition.
front: What does a chemical symbol represent?
back: A chemical symbol represents one atom of an element and also one mole of atoms in molar interpretation.
explanation: Na represents sodium, O represents oxygen.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for atoms, molecules, valency, formulae, equations, empirical formula, and percentage composition.
front: What is atomicity?
back: Atomicity is the number of atoms present in one molecule of an element.
explanation: O2 is diatomic; P4 is tetra-atomic.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for atoms, molecules, valency, formulae, equations, empirical formula, and percentage composition.
front: What is variable valency?
back: Variable valency is the ability of an element to show more than one valency in different compounds.
explanation: Iron shows valency 2 and 3.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for atoms, molecules, valency, formulae, equations, empirical formula, and percentage composition.
front: What is a polyatomic ion?
back: A polyatomic ion is a charged group of two or more atoms acting as a single ion.
explanation: Examples include NH4+, NO3-, SO4²-, and CO3²-.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for atoms, molecules, valency, formulae, equations, empirical formula, and percentage composition.
front: How is the formula of calcium carbonate written from ions?
back: Calcium ion is Ca2+ and carbonate ion is CO3²-, so formula is CaCO3.
explanation: Equal charges cancel in 1:1 ratio.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for atoms, molecules, valency, formulae, equations, empirical formula, and percentage composition.
front: What is the formula of aluminium sulfate?
back: The formula of aluminium sulfate is Al2(SO4)3.
explanation: Criss-cross valencies and use brackets for polyatomic ion.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for atoms, molecules, valency, formulae, equations, empirical formula, and percentage composition.
front: What do state symbols in chemical equations show?
back: State symbols show physical state of substances: solid, liquid, gas, or aqueous.
explanation: They make chemical equations more informative.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for atoms, molecules, valency, formulae, equations, empirical formula, and percentage composition.
front: What is a skeleton equation?
back: A skeleton equation shows reactants and products using formulae but is not yet balanced.
explanation: It becomes complete after balancing coefficients.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for atoms, molecules, valency, formulae, equations, empirical formula, and percentage composition.
front: How are empirical formula and molecular formula related?
back: Molecular formula is an integral multiple of empirical formula.
explanation: n is found from molar mass divided by empirical formula mass.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for atoms, molecules, valency, formulae, equations, empirical formula, and percentage composition.
front: What is the percentage of hydrogen in water approximately?
back: Hydrogen percentage in water is about 11.11 percent by mass.
explanation: Percentage H = 2/18 × 100.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for atoms, molecules, valency, formulae, equations, empirical formula, and percentage composition.
front: What is the percentage of oxygen in water approximately?
back: Oxygen percentage in water is about 88.89 percent by mass.
explanation: Percentage O = 16/18 × 100.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for atoms, molecules, valency, formulae, equations, empirical formula, and percentage composition.
front: Why is relative atomic mass often fractional?
back: Relative atomic mass is fractional because it is a weighted average of isotopic masses.
explanation: Chlorine has relative atomic mass about 35.5 due to isotopes.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for atoms, molecules, valency, formulae, equations, empirical formula, and percentage composition.
front: Name common diatomic molecules.
back: Common diatomic molecules include H2, N2, O2, F2, Cl2, Br2, and I2.
explanation: Remember hydrogen, nitrogen, oxygen, and halogens.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for atoms, molecules, valency, formulae, equations, empirical formula, and percentage composition.
front: What information does a chemical formula give?
back: A chemical formula gives elements present and number or ratio of atoms in a substance.
explanation: Molecular formula gives actual number; empirical formula gives simplest ratio.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for atoms, molecules, valency, formulae, equations, empirical formula, and percentage composition.
front: What does the arrow in a chemical equation mean?
back: The arrow means produces or gives, showing conversion of reactants into products.
explanation: Reactants are written on left and products on right.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for atoms, molecules, valency, formulae, equations, empirical formula, and percentage composition.
front: How is valency related to octet rule?
back: Atoms combine by losing, gaining, or sharing electrons to achieve stable outer shell, often octet configuration.
explanation: Valency reflects the number of electrons involved.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for atoms, molecules, valency, formulae, equations, empirical formula, and percentage composition.
front: Why is ammonium ion considered a radical?
back: Ammonium ion is a group of atoms, NH4+, carrying positive charge and behaving as a single unit.
explanation: It forms salts like NH4Cl.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for atoms, molecules, valency, formulae, equations, empirical formula, and percentage composition.
front: What is molecular mass of CO2?
back: Molecular mass of CO2 is 44.
explanation: Carbon is 12 and oxygen is 16 each.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for atoms, molecules, valency, formulae, equations, empirical formula, and percentage composition.
front: What is formula mass of CaCO3?
back: Formula mass of CaCO3 is 100 approximately.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for atoms, molecules, valency, formulae, equations, empirical formula, and percentage composition.
front: What principle is used to balance chemical equations?
back: Chemical equations are balanced using law of conservation of mass.
explanation: Number of atoms of each element must be equal on both sides.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for atoms, molecules, valency, formulae, equations, empirical formula, and percentage composition.
front: What is a common CEE trap in basic chemistry formula questions?
back: Students confuse empirical formula with molecular formula and forget to simplify ratios.
explanation: Always divide by the smallest mole value and simplify whole numbers.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for atoms, molecules, valency, formulae, equations, empirical formula, and percentage composition.
front: What is the fastest CEE method to revise basic concepts in chemistry?
back: Revise definitions, valencies, radicals, formula writing, equation balancing, empirical formula steps, and percentage composition formula.
explanation: CEE often asks direct definitions and quick formula-based calculations.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for Dalton's theory, stoichiometric laws, Avogadro law, mole concept, limiting reactant, percentage yield, and numerical problems.
front: What is stoichiometry?
back: Stoichiometry is the quantitative study of reactants and products in chemical reactions using balanced equations.
explanation: It connects moles, masses, volumes, and particles.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for Dalton's theory, stoichiometric laws, Avogadro law, mole concept, limiting reactant, percentage yield, and numerical problems.
front: What is the main idea of Dalton's atomic theory?
back: Matter is made of tiny indivisible atoms, and atoms combine in simple whole-number ratios to form compounds.
explanation: Some parts were later modified after discovery of subatomic particles and isotopes.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for Dalton's theory, stoichiometric laws, Avogadro law, mole concept, limiting reactant, percentage yield, and numerical problems.
front: What did Dalton say about compounds?
back: Compounds form when atoms of different elements combine in fixed simple whole-number ratios.
explanation: This supports law of definite proportions.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for Dalton's theory, stoichiometric laws, Avogadro law, mole concept, limiting reactant, percentage yield, and numerical problems.
front: What is law of conservation of mass?
back: Mass is neither created nor destroyed during a chemical reaction.
explanation: Total mass of reactants equals total mass of products.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for Dalton's theory, stoichiometric laws, Avogadro law, mole concept, limiting reactant, percentage yield, and numerical problems.
front: What is law of definite proportions?
back: A pure compound always contains the same elements combined in the same fixed proportion by mass.
explanation: Water always contains hydrogen and oxygen in mass ratio 1:8.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for Dalton's theory, stoichiometric laws, Avogadro law, mole concept, limiting reactant, percentage yield, and numerical problems.
front: What is law of multiple proportions?
back: When two elements form more than one compound, masses of one element combining with fixed mass of the other are in simple whole-number ratios.
explanation: CO and CO2 illustrate this law.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for Dalton's theory, stoichiometric laws, Avogadro law, mole concept, limiting reactant, percentage yield, and numerical problems.
front: What is Gay-Lussac's law of gaseous volumes?
back: Gases react in simple whole-number volume ratios when measured at same temperature and pressure.
explanation: It applies only to gases.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for Dalton's theory, stoichiometric laws, Avogadro law, mole concept, limiting reactant, percentage yield, and numerical problems.
front: What is Avogadro's law?
back: Equal volumes of gases at same temperature and pressure contain equal number of molecules.
explanation: It connects gas volume with moles.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for Dalton's theory, stoichiometric laws, Avogadro law, mole concept, limiting reactant, percentage yield, and numerical problems.
front: What is Avogadro's number?
back: Avogadro's number is 6.022 × 10²³ particles per mole.
explanation: It may represent atoms, molecules, ions, or formula units.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for Dalton's theory, stoichiometric laws, Avogadro law, mole concept, limiting reactant, percentage yield, and numerical problems.
front: What is one mole?
back: One mole is the amount of substance containing 6.022 × 10²³ elementary entities.
explanation: It connects microscopic particles with measurable mass.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for Dalton's theory, stoichiometric laws, Avogadro law, mole concept, limiting reactant, percentage yield, and numerical problems.
front: How do you calculate moles from mass?
back: Moles equal given mass divided by molar mass.
explanation: Use grams and g/mol consistently.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for Dalton's theory, stoichiometric laws, Avogadro law, mole concept, limiting reactant, percentage yield, and numerical problems.
front: How do you calculate number of particles from moles?
back: Number of particles equals moles multiplied by Avogadro's number.
explanation: This applies to atoms, molecules, ions, or formula units.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for Dalton's theory, stoichiometric laws, Avogadro law, mole concept, limiting reactant, percentage yield, and numerical problems.
front: What is molar volume of an ideal gas at STP commonly used in basic chemistry?
back: One mole of ideal gas occupies 22.4 L at STP.
explanation: This is widely used in gas stoichiometry problems.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for Dalton's theory, stoichiometric laws, Avogadro law, mole concept, limiting reactant, percentage yield, and numerical problems.
front: What is mole ratio in a balanced equation?
back: Mole ratio is the ratio of coefficients of substances in a balanced chemical equation.
explanation: It is the heart of stoichiometric calculations.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for Dalton's theory, stoichiometric laws, Avogadro law, mole concept, limiting reactant, percentage yield, and numerical problems.
front: What is the basic method for mass-mass stoichiometry?
back: Convert given mass to moles, use balanced equation mole ratio, then convert required moles to mass.
hint: Mass to mole to mole to mass.
explanation: Never compare masses directly without moles.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for Dalton's theory, stoichiometric laws, Avogadro law, mole concept, limiting reactant, percentage yield, and numerical problems.
front: What is the basic method for mass-volume stoichiometry of gas at STP?
back: Convert mass to moles, use mole ratio, then convert gas moles to volume using 22.4 L per mole.
explanation: Use only for gas volume at STP when applicable.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for Dalton's theory, stoichiometric laws, Avogadro law, mole concept, limiting reactant, percentage yield, and numerical problems.
front: What is limiting reactant?
back: Limiting reactant is the reactant that is completely consumed first and limits the amount of product formed.
explanation: Product amount must be calculated from limiting reactant.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for Dalton's theory, stoichiometric laws, Avogadro law, mole concept, limiting reactant, percentage yield, and numerical problems.
front: What is excess reactant?
back: Excess reactant is the reactant left over after limiting reactant is completely consumed.
explanation: It does not determine maximum product amount.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for Dalton's theory, stoichiometric laws, Avogadro law, mole concept, limiting reactant, percentage yield, and numerical problems.
front: How do you identify limiting reactant?
back: Convert reactants to moles, divide by their stoichiometric coefficients, and the smaller value indicates limiting reactant.
explanation: This method avoids mistakes in multi-reactant problems.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for Dalton's theory, stoichiometric laws, Avogadro law, mole concept, limiting reactant, percentage yield, and numerical problems.
front: What is percentage yield?
back: Percentage yield is actual yield divided by theoretical yield, multiplied by 100.
explanation: It measures efficiency of a reaction.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for Dalton's theory, stoichiometric laws, Avogadro law, mole concept, limiting reactant, percentage yield, and numerical problems.
front: What is theoretical yield?
back: Theoretical yield is maximum amount of product predicted from stoichiometric calculation.
explanation: It assumes complete reaction and no loss.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for Dalton's theory, stoichiometric laws, Avogadro law, mole concept, limiting reactant, percentage yield, and numerical problems.
front: What is actual yield?
back: Actual yield is amount of product actually obtained from an experiment.
explanation: It is usually less than theoretical yield.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for Dalton's theory, stoichiometric laws, Avogadro law, mole concept, limiting reactant, percentage yield, and numerical problems.
front: How many moles are present in 18 g of water?
back: 18 g of water contains 1 mole.
hint: Molar mass of H2O is 18 g/mol.
explanation: n = mass/molar mass = 18/18.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for Dalton's theory, stoichiometric laws, Avogadro law, mole concept, limiting reactant, percentage yield, and numerical problems.
front: How many water molecules are present in 1 mole of water?
back: One mole of water contains 6.022 × 10²³ water molecules.
explanation: One mole of any substance contains Avogadro number of entities.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for Dalton's theory, stoichiometric laws, Avogadro law, mole concept, limiting reactant, percentage yield, and numerical problems.
front: How many oxygen atoms are present in 1 mole of O2 molecules?
back: One mole of O2 contains 2 × 6.022 × 10²³ oxygen atoms.
explanation: Do not confuse molecules with atoms.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for Dalton's theory, stoichiometric laws, Avogadro law, mole concept, limiting reactant, percentage yield, and numerical problems.
front: What volume is occupied by 1 mole of CO2 at STP?
back: One mole of CO2 occupies 22.4 L at STP.
explanation: Gas identity does not change molar volume at same T and P for ideal gas.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for Dalton's theory, stoichiometric laws, Avogadro law, mole concept, limiting reactant, percentage yield, and numerical problems.
front: In 2H2 + O2 -> 2H2O, what is the mole ratio of H2:O2:H2O?
back: The mole ratio is 2:1:2.
explanation: This ratio is used for mole and volume calculations.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for Dalton's theory, stoichiometric laws, Avogadro law, mole concept, limiting reactant, percentage yield, and numerical problems.
front: In N2 + 3H2 -> 2NH3, what is the mole ratio of N2:H2:NH3?
back: The mole ratio is 1:3:2.
explanation: This is a classic stoichiometry pattern.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for Dalton's theory, stoichiometric laws, Avogadro law, mole concept, limiting reactant, percentage yield, and numerical problems.
front: What is molar mass?
back: Molar mass is the mass of one mole of a substance, expressed in g/mol.
explanation: Numerically equal to molecular mass or formula mass in grams.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for Dalton's theory, stoichiometric laws, Avogadro law, mole concept, limiting reactant, percentage yield, and numerical problems.
front: How do you calculate moles of gas from volume at STP?
back: Moles equal gas volume divided by 22.4 L.
explanation: Use this only at STP unless other gas data are given.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for Dalton's theory, stoichiometric laws, Avogadro law, mole concept, limiting reactant, percentage yield, and numerical problems.
front: What is law of reciprocal proportions?
back: When two elements combine separately with a fixed mass of third element, their masses are same or simple multiple of masses in which they combine with each other.

subject: Chemistry

subject: Chemistry

subject: Chemistry

explanation: This gives maximum multiplicity and stability.

subject: Chemistry

back: Electronic configuration is the arrangement of electrons in shells, subshells, and orbitals of an atom.
explanation: It follows Aufbau, Pauli, and Hund rules.

subject: Chemistry

back: Electronegativity is the tendency of an atom in a molecule to attract shared electron pair toward itself.
explanation: Fluorine is the most electronegative element.

subject: Chemistry

front: How does electronegativity vary in the periodic table?
back: Electronegativity generally increases across a period and decreases down a group.
explanation: Fluorine has the highest electronegativity.

subject: Chemistry

front: What is electron affinity?
back: Electron affinity is energy change when an electron is added to an isolated gaseous atom.
explanation: It is often exothermic for non-metals.

subject: Chemistry

front: What is metallic character?
back: Metallic character is tendency of an element to lose electrons and form positive ions.
explanation: It is related to electropositivity.

subject: Chemistry

front: How does metallic character vary in periodic table?
back: Metallic character decreases across a period and increases down a group.
explanation: Francium or cesium show very high metallic character.

subject: Chemistry

front: How does non-metallic character vary in periodic table?
back: Non-metallic character increases across a period and decreases down a group.
explanation: It is opposite to metallic character.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for periodic law, periodic table, blocks, periodic trends, isoelectronic species, and metallic character.
front: What is effective nuclear charge?
back: Effective nuclear charge is net positive attraction experienced by valence electrons after shielding by inner electrons.
explanation: It generally increases across a period.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for periodic law, periodic table, blocks, periodic trends, isoelectronic species, and metallic character.
front: What is shielding effect?
back: Shielding effect is reduction in nuclear attraction on outer electrons due to inner shell electrons.
explanation: It increases down a group.

subject: Chemistry

front: Where are elements with largest atomic size found in periodic table?
back: Largest atomic sizes are found toward the bottom-left of periodic table.
explanation: Atomic size increases down and decreases across a period.

subject: Chemistry

front: Which elements generally have highest ionization potential?
back: Noble gases generally have very high ionization potential due to stable configuration.
explanation: Helium has extremely high first ionization energy.

subject: Chemistry

front: Why is fluorine most electronegative?
back: Fluorine has small size and high effective nuclear charge, so it strongly attracts shared electrons.
explanation: It is at top-right among reactive non-metals.

subject: Chemistry

back: Period number indicates the highest principal energy level occupied by electrons.
explanation: Elements in period 3 have valence electrons in n = 3 shell.

subject: Chemistry

front: Why do elements in the same group show similar properties?
back: They have similar valence shell electronic configuration.
explanation: Chemical properties mainly depend on valence electrons.

subject: Chemistry

back: Alkali metals are group 1 elements except hydrogen, with one valence electron.
explanation: They are highly reactive and form +1 ions.

subject: Chemistry

back: Alkaline earth metals are group 2 elements with two valence electrons.
explanation: They commonly form +2 ions.

subject: Chemistry

back: Halogens are group 17 elements with seven valence electrons.
explanation: They commonly form -1 ions.

subject: Chemistry

back: Noble gases have completely filled valence shells, making them very stable.
explanation: They have high ionization energy and low reactivity.

subject: Chemistry

back: Periodicity is caused by repeated similar valence electronic configurations at regular intervals.
explanation: Atomic number arrangement reveals this repetition.

subject: Chemistry

explanation: Atomic size depends on bonding environment.

back: Cl- ion is larger than Cl atom.
explanation: Adding electron increases repulsion and expands size.

subject: Chemistry

back: Halogens need one electron to complete octet, so they readily accept electron.
explanation: They release energy during electron gain.

subject: Chemistry

back: Electropositive character is tendency of an atom to lose electrons and form cations.
explanation: It increases down a group.

subject: Chemistry

front: Summarize major trends across a period.
back: Across a period, atomic size decreases, ionization energy and electronegativity increase, and metallic character decreases.
explanation: Effective nuclear charge increases across period.

subject: Chemistry

back: Down a group, atomic size increases, ionization energy and electronegativity decrease, and metallic character increases.
explanation: New shells and shielding increase down group.

subject: Chemistry

explanation: They show variable oxidation states.

subject: Chemistry

explanation: Lanthanides fill 4f and actinides fill 5f orbitals.

explanation: In isoelectronic series, size decreases as nuclear charge increases.

subject: Chemistry

explanation: Always connect trend with nuclear attraction and electron configuration.

explanation: CEE frequently asks order-based and reason-based periodic trend questions.

front: What is oxidation in classical concept?
back: Oxidation is addition of oxygen or removal of hydrogen.
explanation: Example: burning of carbon to CO2 is oxidation.

subject: Chemistry

front: What is reduction in classical concept?
back: Reduction is removal of oxygen or addition of hydrogen.
explanation: Reduction is opposite of oxidation.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for oxidation, reduction, oxidation number, redox balancing by oxidation number and ion-electron methods, and applications.
front: What is oxidation in electronic concept?
back: Oxidation is loss of electrons.
explanation: Species losing electrons is oxidized.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for oxidation, reduction, oxidation number, redox balancing by oxidation number and ion-electron methods, and applications.
front: What is reduction in electronic concept?
back: Reduction is gain of electrons.
explanation: Species gaining electrons is reduced.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for oxidation, reduction, oxidation number, redox balancing by oxidation number and ion-electron methods, and applications.
front: What is an oxidizing agent?
back: An oxidizing agent causes oxidation of another species and itself gets reduced.
explanation: It gains electrons.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for oxidation, reduction, oxidation number, redox balancing by oxidation number and ion-electron methods, and applications.
front: What is a reducing agent?
back: A reducing agent causes reduction of another species and itself gets oxidized.
explanation: It loses electrons.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for oxidation, reduction, oxidation number, redox balancing by oxidation number and ion-electron methods, and applications.
front: What is oxidation number?
back: Oxidation number is the apparent charge assigned to an atom in a compound or ion based on electron accounting rules.
explanation: It helps identify oxidation and reduction.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for oxidation, reduction, oxidation number, redox balancing by oxidation number and ion-electron methods, and applications.
front: What is oxidation number of an element in free state?
back: Oxidation number of an element in free state is zero.
explanation: Examples: Na, O2, H2, Cl2 all have oxidation number zero.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for oxidation, reduction, oxidation number, redox balancing by oxidation number and ion-electron methods, and applications.
front: What is oxidation number of a monoatomic ion?
back: Oxidation number of a monoatomic ion equals its charge.
explanation: Na+ is +1 and Cl- is -1.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for oxidation, reduction, oxidation number, redox balancing by oxidation number and ion-electron methods, and applications.
front: What is usual oxidation number of oxygen?
back: Oxygen usually has oxidation number -2.
explanation: Exceptions include peroxides where oxygen is -1.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for oxidation, reduction, oxidation number, redox balancing by oxidation number and ion-electron methods, and applications.
front: What is usual oxidation number of hydrogen?
back: Hydrogen usually has oxidation number +1 with non-metals and -1 in metal hydrides.
explanation: In NaH, hydrogen is -1.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for oxidation, reduction, oxidation number, redox balancing by oxidation number and ion-electron methods, and applications.
front: What is sum of oxidation numbers in a neutral compound?
back: Sum of oxidation numbers of all atoms in a neutral compound is zero.
explanation: Use this rule to calculate unknown oxidation number.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for oxidation, reduction, oxidation number, redox balancing by oxidation number and ion-electron methods, and applications.
front: What is sum of oxidation numbers in a polyatomic ion?
back: Sum of oxidation numbers equals the overall charge of the ion.
explanation: For SO4²-, total is -2.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for oxidation, reduction, oxidation number, redox balancing by oxidation number and ion-electron methods, and applications.
front: What is oxidation number of sulfur in SO4²-?
back: Oxidation number of sulfur in SO4²- is +6.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for oxidation, reduction, oxidation number, redox balancing by oxidation number and ion-electron methods, and applications.
front: What is oxidation number of Mn in MnO4-?
back: Oxidation number of Mn in MnO4- is +7.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for oxidation, reduction, oxidation number, redox balancing by oxidation number and ion-electron methods, and applications.
front: What is oxidation number of Cr in Cr2O7²-?
back: Oxidation number of Cr in Cr2O7²- is +6.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for oxidation, reduction, oxidation number, redox balancing by oxidation number and ion-electron methods, and applications.
front: How does oxidation number change during oxidation and reduction?
back: Oxidation increases oxidation number, while reduction decreases oxidation number.
explanation: Track oxidation number changes to identify redox process.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for oxidation, reduction, oxidation number, redox balancing by oxidation number and ion-electron methods, and applications.
front: How do you identify whether a reaction is redox?
back: Check if oxidation numbers of any elements change during the reaction.
explanation: If no oxidation number changes, it is not redox.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for oxidation, reduction, oxidation number, redox balancing by oxidation number and ion-electron methods, and applications.
front: What is the main principle of oxidation number method?
back: Total increase in oxidation number must equal total decrease in oxidation number.
explanation: Then balance atoms and charges as needed.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for oxidation, reduction, oxidation number, redox balancing by oxidation number and ion-electron methods, and applications.
front: What is ion-electron method?
back: Ion-electron method balances redox reactions by separating oxidation and reduction half-reactions and balancing electrons.
explanation: It is especially useful in acidic and basic medium.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for oxidation, reduction, oxidation number, redox balancing by oxidation number and ion-electron methods, and applications.
front: What is a half-reaction?
back: A half-reaction shows either oxidation or reduction part of a redox reaction separately.
explanation: Electrons appear in half-reactions.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for oxidation, reduction, oxidation number, redox balancing by oxidation number and ion-electron methods, and applications.
front: In acidic medium, what species are used to balance oxygen and hydrogen?
back: In acidic medium, oxygen is balanced using H2O and hydrogen is balanced using H+ ions.
explanation: Then balance charge using electrons.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for oxidation, reduction, oxidation number, redox balancing by oxidation number and ion-electron methods, and applications.
front: In basic medium, what species are used during redox balancing?
back: In basic medium, H2O and OH- ions are used to balance hydrogen and oxygen after balancing charge.
explanation: A common method is to balance as acidic first, then neutralize H+ with OH-.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for oxidation, reduction, oxidation number, redox balancing by oxidation number and ion-electron methods, and applications.
front: In a redox reaction, why must electrons lost equal electrons gained?
back: Electrons cannot be created or destroyed, so total electrons lost in oxidation must equal total electrons gained in reduction.
explanation: This is the basis of redox balancing.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for oxidation, reduction, oxidation number, redox balancing by oxidation number and ion-electron methods, and applications.
front: What is disproportionation reaction?
back: Disproportionation is a redox reaction in which the same element is both oxidized and reduced.
explanation: It starts from an intermediate oxidation state.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for oxidation, reduction, oxidation number, redox balancing by oxidation number and ion-electron methods, and applications.
front: What is comproportionation reaction?
back: Comproportionation is a redox reaction where two species of same element in different oxidation states form a product with intermediate oxidation state.
explanation: It is also called synproportionation.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for oxidation, reduction, oxidation number, redox balancing by oxidation number and ion-electron methods, and applications.
front: Name common oxidizing agents.
back: Common oxidizing agents include KMnO4, K2Cr2O7, HNO3, O2, Cl2, and H2O2 in some reactions.
explanation: They get reduced during reaction.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for oxidation, reduction, oxidation number, redox balancing by oxidation number and ion-electron methods, and applications.
front: Name common reducing agents.
back: Common reducing agents include H2, CO, Zn, Fe2+, SO2, and H2S.
explanation: They get oxidized during reaction.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for oxidation, reduction, oxidation number, redox balancing by oxidation number and ion-electron methods, and applications.
front: Name applications of redox reactions.
back: Redox reactions are used in batteries, corrosion, respiration, combustion, metallurgy, titration, and bleaching.
explanation: Many biological and industrial processes are redox.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for oxidation, reduction, oxidation number, redox balancing by oxidation number and ion-electron methods, and applications.
front: Why is rusting of iron a redox reaction?
back: Iron is oxidized while oxygen is reduced in presence of moisture, forming hydrated iron oxide.
explanation: Rusting is electrochemical corrosion.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for oxidation, reduction, oxidation number, redox balancing by oxidation number and ion-electron methods, and applications.
front: Why is combustion a redox reaction?
back: Combustion involves oxidation of fuel and reduction of oxygen.
explanation: It releases heat and often light.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for oxidation, reduction, oxidation number, redox balancing by oxidation number and ion-electron methods, and applications.
front: How do batteries use redox reactions?
back: Batteries convert chemical energy into electrical energy through spontaneous redox reactions.
explanation: Oxidation occurs at anode and reduction at cathode.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for oxidation, reduction, oxidation number, redox balancing by oxidation number and ion-electron methods, and applications.
front: Why can chlorine show multiple oxidation states?
back: Chlorine can gain, lose, or share electrons in different compounds, giving oxidation states from -1 to positive values.
explanation: In Cl-, chlorine is -1; in oxyacids it can be positive.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for oxidation, reduction, oxidation number, redox balancing by oxidation number and ion-electron methods, and applications.
front: What is oxidation number of oxygen in peroxides?
back: Oxygen has oxidation number -1 in peroxides.
explanation: In H2O2, oxygen is -1.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for oxidation, reduction, oxidation number, redox balancing by oxidation number and ion-electron methods, and applications.
front: What is oxidation number of oxygen in superoxides?
back: Oxygen has average oxidation number -1/2 in superoxides.
explanation: This is an exception to usual oxygen oxidation number.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for oxidation, reduction, oxidation number, redox balancing by oxidation number and ion-electron methods, and applications.
front: What is oxidation number of fluorine in compounds?
back: Fluorine always has oxidation number -1 in compounds.
explanation: It does not show positive oxidation state in normal compounds.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for oxidation, reduction, oxidation number, redox balancing by oxidation number and ion-electron methods, and applications.
front: What is oxidation number of alkali metals in compounds?
back: Alkali metals usually have oxidation number +1 in compounds.
explanation: Examples: NaCl, KNO3, Li2O.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for oxidation, reduction, oxidation number, redox balancing by oxidation number and ion-electron methods, and applications.
front: What is oxidation number of alkaline earth metals in compounds?
back: Alkaline earth metals usually have oxidation number +2 in compounds.
explanation: Examples: MgCl2, CaO, BaSO4.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for oxidation, reduction, oxidation number, redox balancing by oxidation number and ion-electron methods, and applications.
front: In half-reaction balancing, why are electrons added?
back: Electrons are added to balance charge on both sides of a half-reaction.
explanation: Electrons must cancel when half-reactions are added.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for oxidation, reduction, oxidation number, redox balancing by oxidation number and ion-electron methods, and applications.
front: On which side are electrons written in oxidation half-reaction?
back: Electrons are written on product side in oxidation half-reaction.
explanation: Loss of electrons means electrons appear as products.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for oxidation, reduction, oxidation number, redox balancing by oxidation number and ion-electron methods, and applications.
front: On which side are electrons written in reduction half-reaction?
back: Electrons are written on reactant side in reduction half-reaction.
explanation: Gained electrons are consumed.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for oxidation, reduction, oxidation number, redox balancing by oxidation number and ion-electron methods, and applications.
front: What does MnO4- usually reduce to in acidic medium?
back: Permanganate ion MnO4- usually reduces to Mn2+ in acidic medium.
explanation: Mn changes from +7 to +2.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for oxidation, reduction, oxidation number, redox balancing by oxidation number and ion-electron methods, and applications.
front: What does Cr2O7²- usually reduce to in acidic medium?
back: Dichromate ion Cr2O7²- reduces to Cr3+ in acidic medium.
explanation: Chromium changes from +6 to +3.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for oxidation, reduction, oxidation number, redox balancing by oxidation number and ion-electron methods, and applications.
front: What does LEO GER mean in redox?
back: LEO GER means Loss of Electrons is Oxidation and Gain of Electrons is Reduction.
explanation: It is equivalent to OIL RIG.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for oxidation, reduction, oxidation number, redox balancing by oxidation number and ion-electron methods, and applications.
front: Is acid-base neutralization always a redox reaction?
back: No, neutralization is usually not redox because oxidation numbers do not change.
explanation: H+ and OH- form water without electron transfer.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for oxidation, reduction, oxidation number, redox balancing by oxidation number and ion-electron methods, and applications.
front: How is bleaching related to redox?
back: Bleaching often involves oxidation or reduction of colored substances into colorless products.
explanation: Chlorine and hydrogen peroxide can act as bleaching agents.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for oxidation, reduction, oxidation number, redox balancing by oxidation number and ion-electron methods, and applications.
front: How are redox reactions used in metallurgy?
back: Metal ores are reduced to extract metals, while reducing agents get oxidized.
explanation: Carbon monoxide reduces iron oxide in blast furnace.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for oxidation, reduction, oxidation number, redox balancing by oxidation number and ion-electron methods, and applications.
front: What is a common CEE trap in redox reactions?
back: Students identify oxidizing agent incorrectly; the oxidizing agent gets reduced, not oxidized.
explanation: Oxidizing agent accepts electrons.

back: Revise oxidation-reduction definitions, oxidation number rules, agent identification, balancing methods, and common applications like corrosion and batteries.
explanation: CEE often asks oxidation number calculation, oxidizing-reducing agent, and redox balancing logic.

front: What is the kinetic theory of gases?
back: Kinetic theory explains gas behavior based on rapid random motion of gas molecules.
explanation: It connects pressure, volume, temperature, and molecular motion.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for gases, liquids, solutions, solids, crystallization, unit cells, crystal systems, Bravais lattices, and crystalline solid classification.
front: What causes pressure of a gas?
back: Gas pressure is caused by collisions of gas molecules with the walls of the container.
explanation: More frequent or stronger collisions increase pressure.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for gases, liquids, solutions, solids, crystallization, unit cells, crystal systems, Bravais lattices, and crystalline solid classification.
front: How is temperature related to kinetic energy of gas molecules?
back: Absolute temperature is directly proportional to average kinetic energy of gas molecules.
explanation: This is a key idea of kinetic theory.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for gases, liquids, solutions, solids, crystallization, unit cells, crystal systems, Bravais lattices, and crystalline solid classification.
front: What is Boyle's law?
back: At constant temperature, volume of a fixed mass of gas is inversely proportional to pressure.
explanation: PV remains constant.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for gases, liquids, solutions, solids, crystallization, unit cells, crystal systems, Bravais lattices, and crystalline solid classification.
front: What is Charles' law?
back: At constant pressure, volume of a fixed mass of gas is directly proportional to absolute temperature.
explanation: Temperature must be in kelvin.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for gases, liquids, solutions, solids, crystallization, unit cells, crystal systems, Bravais lattices, and crystalline solid classification.
front: What is Gay-Lussac's pressure law?
back: At constant volume, pressure of a fixed mass of gas is directly proportional to absolute temperature.
explanation: Heating a closed container increases pressure.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for gases, liquids, solutions, solids, crystallization, unit cells, crystal systems, Bravais lattices, and crystalline solid classification.
front: What is Avogadro's law for gases?
back: At same temperature and pressure, equal volumes of gases contain equal number of molecules.
explanation: Volume is directly proportional to number of moles.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for gases, liquids, solutions, solids, crystallization, unit cells, crystal systems, Bravais lattices, and crystalline solid classification.
front: What is the ideal gas equation?
back: The ideal gas equation is PV = nRT.
explanation: It combines Boyle's, Charles', and Avogadro's laws.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for gases, liquids, solutions, solids, crystallization, unit cells, crystal systems, Bravais lattices, and crystalline solid classification.
front: What is the combined gas equation?
back: For a fixed amount of gas, P1V1/T1 = P2V2/T2.
explanation: Temperature must be in kelvin.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for gases, liquids, solutions, solids, crystallization, unit cells, crystal systems, Bravais lattices, and crystalline solid classification.
front: What is an ideal gas?
back: An ideal gas is a hypothetical gas that obeys gas laws exactly at all temperatures and pressures.
explanation: Its molecules have negligible volume and no intermolecular attraction.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for gases, liquids, solutions, solids, crystallization, unit cells, crystal systems, Bravais lattices, and crystalline solid classification.
front: Why do real gases deviate from ideal behavior?
back: Real gases deviate because their molecules have finite volume and intermolecular forces.
explanation: Deviation is greater at high pressure and low temperature.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for gases, liquids, solutions, solids, crystallization, unit cells, crystal systems, Bravais lattices, and crystalline solid classification.
front: When do real gases behave most ideally?
back: Real gases behave most ideally at low pressure and high temperature.
explanation: Intermolecular forces become less significant.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for gases, liquids, solutions, solids, crystallization, unit cells, crystal systems, Bravais lattices, and crystalline solid classification.
front: What is vapour pressure?
back: Vapour pressure is the pressure exerted by vapour in equilibrium with its liquid at a given temperature.
explanation: It increases with temperature.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for gases, liquids, solutions, solids, crystallization, unit cells, crystal systems, Bravais lattices, and crystalline solid classification.
front: What is boiling point?
back: Boiling point is the temperature at which vapour pressure of a liquid equals external pressure.
explanation: Lower external pressure lowers boiling point.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for gases, liquids, solutions, solids, crystallization, unit cells, crystal systems, Bravais lattices, and crystalline solid classification.
front: What is surface tension?
back: Surface tension is the tendency of liquid surface to contract and behave like a stretched membrane.
explanation: It is due to cohesive force between liquid molecules.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for gases, liquids, solutions, solids, crystallization, unit cells, crystal systems, Bravais lattices, and crystalline solid classification.
front: What is viscosity?
back: Viscosity is resistance of a liquid to flow.
explanation: Honey is more viscous than water.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for gases, liquids, solutions, solids, crystallization, unit cells, crystal systems, Bravais lattices, and crystalline solid classification.
front: What is a liquid crystal?
back: A liquid crystal is a state of matter with properties between liquid and crystalline solid.
hint: Flows like liquid, ordered like crystal.
explanation: It is used in LCD displays.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for gases, liquids, solutions, solids, crystallization, unit cells, crystal systems, Bravais lattices, and crystalline solid classification.
front: What is a solution?
back: A solution is a homogeneous mixture of two or more substances.
explanation: It contains solute and solvent.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for gases, liquids, solutions, solids, crystallization, unit cells, crystal systems, Bravais lattices, and crystalline solid classification.
front: What are solute and solvent?
back: Solute is the substance dissolved, while solvent is the substance that dissolves the solute.
explanation: In salt water, salt is solute and water is solvent.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for gases, liquids, solutions, solids, crystallization, unit cells, crystal systems, Bravais lattices, and crystalline solid classification.
front: What is solubility?
back: Solubility is the maximum amount of solute that dissolves in a given amount of solvent at a specified temperature.
explanation: It depends on nature of solute, solvent, and temperature.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for gases, liquids, solutions, solids, crystallization, unit cells, crystal systems, Bravais lattices, and crystalline solid classification.
front: What does a solubility curve show?
back: A solubility curve shows how solubility of a substance changes with temperature.
explanation: It helps identify saturated and unsaturated conditions.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for gases, liquids, solutions, solids, crystallization, unit cells, crystal systems, Bravais lattices, and crystalline solid classification.
front: What is a crystalline solid?
back: A crystalline solid has regular, repeating three-dimensional arrangement of particles.
explanation: Examples include NaCl, diamond, and quartz.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for gases, liquids, solutions, solids, crystallization, unit cells, crystal systems, Bravais lattices, and crystalline solid classification.
front: What is an amorphous solid?
back: An amorphous solid lacks long-range regular arrangement of particles.
explanation: Glass, rubber, and plastic are examples.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for gases, liquids, solutions, solids, crystallization, unit cells, crystal systems, Bravais lattices, and crystalline solid classification.
front: How do crystalline and amorphous solids differ?
back: Crystalline solids have sharp melting point and regular arrangement, while amorphous solids soften over a range and lack long-range order.
explanation: Crystalline solids are anisotropic; amorphous solids are isotropic.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for gases, liquids, solutions, solids, crystallization, unit cells, crystal systems, Bravais lattices, and crystalline solid classification.
front: What is efflorescence?
back: Efflorescence is loss of water of crystallization from a hydrated salt on exposure to air.
explanation: Washing soda can show efflorescence.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for gases, liquids, solutions, solids, crystallization, unit cells, crystal systems, Bravais lattices, and crystalline solid classification.
front: What is deliquescence?
back: Deliquescence is absorption of moisture from air until the solid dissolves in absorbed water.
explanation: CaCl2 and NaOH are deliquescent substances.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for gases, liquids, solutions, solids, crystallization, unit cells, crystal systems, Bravais lattices, and crystalline solid classification.
front: What is a hygroscopic solid?
back: A hygroscopic solid absorbs moisture from air but does not necessarily dissolve in it.
explanation: Concentrated sulfuric acid and silica gel are common drying agents.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for gases, liquids, solutions, solids, crystallization, unit cells, crystal systems, Bravais lattices, and crystalline solid classification.
front: What is crystallization?
back: Crystallization is formation of pure solid crystals from a solution or melt.
explanation: It is used for purification of solids.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for gases, liquids, solutions, solids, crystallization, unit cells, crystal systems, Bravais lattices, and crystalline solid classification.
front: What is water of crystallization?
back: Water of crystallization is fixed number of water molecules chemically associated with a crystalline salt.
explanation: CuSO4·5H2O contains five water molecules per formula unit.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for gases, liquids, solutions, solids, crystallization, unit cells, crystal systems, Bravais lattices, and crystalline solid classification.
front: What is crystal growth?
back: Crystal growth is increase in size of a crystal by orderly deposition of particles on its surface.
explanation: Slow cooling often helps form larger crystals.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for gases, liquids, solutions, solids, crystallization, unit cells, crystal systems, Bravais lattices, and crystalline solid classification.
front: What is a unit cell?
back: A unit cell is the smallest repeating unit of a crystal lattice that represents the whole crystal structure.
explanation: Repeating unit cells build the crystal.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for gases, liquids, solutions, solids, crystallization, unit cells, crystal systems, Bravais lattices, and crystalline solid classification.
front: What is a crystal lattice?
back: A crystal lattice is a regular three-dimensional arrangement of points representing positions of particles in a crystal.
explanation: Each lattice point has identical surroundings.

subject: Chemistry
deck_description: High-yield Physical Chemistry flashcards for gases, liquids, solutions, solids, crystallization, unit cells, crystal systems, Bravais lattices, and crystalline solid classification.
front: What is a simple or primitive unit cell?
back: A primitive unit cell has particles only at the corners of the unit cell.
explanation: It effectively contains one particle per unit cell.

front: What is a body-centered unit cell?
